newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ROMA BEGIN DECISIVE DECEMBER AGAINST FIORENTINA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMA BEGIN DECISIVE DECEMBER AGAINST FIORENTINA.

text.p: AS Roma and Fiorentina, two of the many pretenders to the Italian throne, meet in a potentially decisive clash at the Olympic Stadium in Rome on Sunday night.
The Serie A table currently has an unusual look to it, with provincial side Vicenza on top, one point clear of Bologna and Internazionale in joint second.
In what appears to be the most open Italian title race for more than a decade, Roma and Fiorentina are two of at least six sides which can still consider themselves championship contenders.
Roma come into the game in seventh place but are only five points behind leaders Vicenza, while they are just one point behind Juventus and on the same points as champions AC Milan.
Tenth placed Fiorentina are also not out of the hunt, just one point behind Roma in a crowded table which sees the top 14 sides separated by just eight points.
For Roma, Sunday's game initiates a probably decisive quartet of December matches against Fiorentina, Lazio, Napoli and Atalanta, all at home.
Already eliminated from both the Italian and UEFA Cups, Roma have only the league championship left as a seasonal objective.
Roma attacker Francesco Totti believes this fact will give his side greater movtivation than Fiorentina, who are in the quarter-finals of the Cup Winners' Cup.

"For us the league championship is everything while Fiorentina are still going in the Cup Winners' Cup and therefore have something else to play for. We've got to win on Sunday to stick close to the big names."
But Fiorentina striker Francesco Baiano says his side are serious championship challengers and will not be taking things easy at the Olympic Stadium.

"Roma are a good side but we play our best soccer against the big sides," he said. "If the league was just Inter, AC Milan, Juventus, Lazio, Roma and Parma, we would be the number one title challengers".
Both sides will be at close to full strength on Sunday with Totti playing behind Marco Delvecchio and Argentine Abel Balbo in a three man attack.
Swede Jonas Thern returns to midfield in place of the suspended Luigi Di Biagio while Brazilian Aldair leads the defence.
Roma's Uruguyan striker Daniel Fonseca starts the game on the bench while Argentine defender Roberto Trotta is still recovering from a knee cartilege operation.
Fiorentina again look to their all foreign attack of Brazilian Oliveira, Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Portuguese playmaker Rui Costa.
